mainTopic: Supporting daughters from land versus movable property, and the court-set conditions of the כתובה
overview: This amud opens by finishing an argument about dates still on a palm tree. They count as land as long as they still need the tree. Next, רבא tells the people handling an estate to give an orphan boy extra so his sister can be supported. He defends this with a קל וחומר: we would buy the boy a maidservant, so we can certainly support his sister. A ברייתא then brings a מחלוקת. רבי allows support from both land and movable property. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר allows it only from land. The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, as רבא ruled. A new משנה follows: the minimum כתובה, the guarantee on all of the husband's property, and the duty to redeem a captive wife all apply even if never written, as a תנאי בית דין. A husband may divorce his wife to avoid paying for her healing, but not to avoid redeeming her. The גמרא shows that the משנה's opening fits רבי מאיר, while its field clause seems to fit רבי יהודה, and it starts quoting the source for their argument about a missing guarantee clause.

steps.title: Dates about to be cut already count as cut
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף: dates that are ready to be harvested should count as movable property, not land.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, anything that is about to be cut is treated as if it were already cut!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a challenge to the ruling just before this, that dates still on the palm tree can be used for a daughter's מזונות. The challenge says ripe dates should be treated as already picked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A daughter's מזונות can be collected only from land, not from movable property. There is a known rule, כל העומד לגזוז כגזוז דמי: produce ready to be harvested is treated as if it were already harvested. If so, ripe dates count as movable property, and she should not be able to collect from them.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything about to be cut is treated as already cut

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the dates are worth money. The question is which category they belong to: land, which can be used for her support, or movable property, which cannot.

phrases.english: Ultimately, anything that is about to be cut
phrases.notes: This is אביי pushing back on רב יוסף's ruling just before this, about dates still on the palm tree.

phrases.english: is considered as already cut!

steps.triggerLanguage: סוף סוף, כל העומד לגזוז כגזוז דמי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's ruling from the previous section, which allowed collecting from dates on the tree.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling that a daughter's מזונות may be collected from dates still on the palm tree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ripe dates are 'about to be cut', so they count as movable property, and מזונות cannot be collected from movable property.

steps.title: The dates still need the tree
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that he meant dates that are not fully ripe and still need the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: I was talking about dates that still need the palm tree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains that his ruling was about dates that still need to keep growing on the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule כל העומד לגזוז applies only to produce that is fully ready to be cut. Dates that still draw food from the tree are not 'about to be cut', so they still count as part of the land. That makes them fine to use for the daughter's מזונות.
steps.whatToRemember: Produce still growing on the tree counts as land. Once it is fully ready to be cut, it is treated as movable property.

phrases.english: I spoke of dates that still need the palm tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by narrowing which case was meant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed to cover even ripe dates that are ready to be harvested.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling covers only dates that still need the tree, so they still count as land.

steps.title: רבא gives the orphan boy extra for his sister
steps.stepSummary: An orphan boy and girl come before רבא, and he rules that the boy should get more so the girl can be supported too.
steps.simpleTranslation: An orphan boy and an orphan girl came before רבא. רבא said: Give more to the orphan boy, so there is enough for the orphan girl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a ruling רבא gave for two orphans. This ruling will be challenged in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the son inherits and the daughter is supported from the estate. רבא tells them to give the boy a larger share from the estate, so that the girl will be supported along with him.

phrases.english: There was a certain orphan boy and orphan girl
who came before Rava.
Rava said to them:
Increase the amount for the orphan boy for the sake of the orphan girl.

steps.triggerLanguage: ההוא יתום ויתומה דאתו לקמיה דרבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story that is related to the topic of supporting daughters from an estate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court gives the orphan boy extra from the estate so that his sister will also be supported.

steps.title: But רבא himself said only from land
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן challenge רבא with his own ruling: support is collected only from land, never from movable property.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רבא: But you yourself said that we collect from land and not from movable property, whether for food, for the כתובה, or for a daughter's marriage money!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן point out that רבא's ruling seems to contradict his own earlier rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא himself ruled that support, a כתובה, and a daughter's פרנסה are collected only from land, not from movable property. In this case the estate apparently had only movable property, so supporting the girl from it seems to go against his own rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master, a respectful way to say 'you'
Money given to a daughter for her marriage

phrases.english: The Sages said to Rava:
But isn't the Master the one who said
from land and not from movable property,
phrases.notes: The רבנן are assuming this estate had only movable property, so it looks like nothing should go to the girl.

phrases.english: whether for sustenance, whether for the marriage contract,
and whether for livelihood!

steps.triggerLanguage: אמרי ליה רבנן לרבא והא מר הוא דאמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in step 3 using his own earlier rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling to support the orphan girl from the estate
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא ruled that these payments come only from land, but here the girl is being supported from movable property.

steps.title: Like buying him a maidservant, but even better
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers: we would spend estate money on a maidservant for the boy, so we can certainly spend it on his sister, who helps him and is also family.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If the boy wanted a maidservant to serve him, wouldn't we give him one? All the more so here, where there are two good reasons.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his ruling with a קל וחומר. He shows that this is really spending money for the boy's own benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא is not collecting the girl's מזונות as a claim against the estate. Spending the boy's own money to buy him a servant would be allowed. Supporting his sister is even better, since she serves him and she is also his sister. So the rule about land and movable property does not apply here.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's ruling is not an exception to 'only from land'. It is spending the boy's own money in a way that benefits him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even where a claim cannot be collected, the court may use an orphan's money for something that benefits the orphan himself.

phrases.english: He said to them:
If he wanted a maidservant to serve him,
would we not give him one?
All the more so here,
where there are two benefits.
phrases.notes: The two: she will serve him, and she is his own sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר להו אילו רצה שפחה לשמשו מי לא יהבינן ליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Supporting the girl looked like collecting מזונות from movable property.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is really spending the boy's money for his own benefit, which is even better than buying him a servant.

steps.title: רבי: both land and movables can be used for support
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי: both land and movable property can be taken to support a widow and daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Both property that has a guarantee and property that does not have a guarantee can be taken for the support of a wife and daughters. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a מחלוקת. This step gives the first opinion, רבי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נכסים שיש להן אחריות means land, which stands behind a debt. נכסים שאין להן אחריות means movable property. רבי holds that both kinds can be used to support the widow and daughters, which is more lenient than the rule 'only from land' seen above.

keyTerms.meaning: Property with a guarantee, meaning land
Property without a guarantee, meaning movable property
We take out, collect from the heirs

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Both property that has a guarantee,
phrases.notes: This means land, which can always be seized to pay a debt.

phrases.english: and property that does not have a guarantee —
are taken out for the sustenance of a wife and for daughters,
these are the words of Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנו רבנן אחד נכסים שיש להן אחריות ואחד נכסים שאין להן אחריות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section: a ברייתא on which kinds of property can be used for support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, both land and movable property are taken from the heirs to support a widow and daughters.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר on taking land from heirs
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says land is taken from sons for daughters, from older daughters for younger daughters, and from older sons for younger sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Property that has a guarantee is taken for the daughters from the sons, for daughters from daughters, and for sons from sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the second opinion, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's. He lists cases where land is taken from heirs who already took it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He talks specifically about land (נכסים שיש להן אחריות). Land is taken from the sons to support the daughters. If there were only daughters, land is taken from older daughters who took the estate, so younger daughters get an equal share. The same applies to older sons and younger sons.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with רבי here

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
property that has a guarantee —
is taken out for the daughters from the sons,
and for daughters from daughters,
phrases.notes: If there were only daughters, the older ones who took the estate must give an equal share to the younger ones.

phrases.english: and for sons from sons.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר אומר נכסים שיש להן אחריות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the מחלוקת in the ברייתא started in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Land is taken from heirs who took it: for daughters from sons, for younger daughters from older daughters, and for younger sons from older sons.

steps.title: Land goes from daughters to sons only when the estate is large
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר continues. When the estate is large, land is taken from the daughters for the sons. When it is small, it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And land is taken from the daughters for the sons when the estate is large, but not when the estate is small.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is still speaking from Step 7. He adds a rule about when land moves from the daughters to the sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons are the real heirs, so when there is plenty of land, the extra land beyond the daughters' support goes to them. When there is only a little land, the daughters' support comes first, so nothing is taken from them for the sons.

keyTerms.meaning: A large estate, with enough for everyone
A small estate, without enough for everyone

phrases.english: And land is taken for the sons from the daughters
when the estate is large,
but it is not taken for the sons from the daughters
when the estate is small.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same statement of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר from Step 7 about land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From land: daughters give to sons only in a large estate; in a small estate the daughters keep it for their support.

steps.title: Movable property can go from daughters to sons, never from sons to daughters
steps.stepSummary: For movable property, a fair share is taken back from older sons for younger sons, from older daughters for younger daughters, and from daughters for sons. It is never taken from sons for daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Property that has no guarantee (movable property) is taken from sons for sons, from daughters for daughters, and from daughters for sons, but never from sons for daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר now gives the rule for movable property, which works differently from land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Daughters have no claim to support from movable property at all. So if they grabbed some, it is taken back for the sons, who are the heirs. But the sons never have to hand movable property over to the daughters. This is exactly where he disagrees with רבי in Step 6, who allowed movable property to be used for support too.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that cannot serve as a guarantee, meaning movable property
A guarantee or lien on property
We take it away (from whoever is holding it)

steps.confusionAlert: In this step 'from sons for sons' and 'from daughters for daughters' means taking from older siblings to give younger siblings a fair share. It is not a contradiction.

phrases.english: Property that has no guarantee
phrases.notes: This means movable things like money or furniture, which can't be held as security the way land can.

phrases.english: is taken from the sons for the sons,
and from the daughters for the daughters,
and from the daughters for the sons.
But not from the sons for the daughters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's statement by moving from land to movable property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Daughters cannot take their support from movable property; movable property can go to sons but never from sons to daughters.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, as רבא ruled
steps.stepSummary: Normally the הלכה follows רבי against a single colleague. Here it follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, because רבא ruled that women collect only from land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though we usually rule like רבי against his colleague, here the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. For רבא said: the הלכה is that a woman collects from land and not from movable property, whether for her כתובה, her מזונות, or her פרנסה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the argument between רבי (Step 6) and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר (Step 7). It explains why we do not follow the usual rule of ruling like רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that רבי wins against one colleague. רבא's ruling, though, says payments are made only from land, never from movable property, and that matches רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. This also fits what the רבנן said to רבא back in Step 4, that support comes only from land.

keyTerms.meaning: The general rule that the הלכה follows רבי against one colleague

steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: a כתובה, a widow's or daughter's מזונות, and a daughter's פרנסה are all collected only from land, not from movable property, following רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a general rule like 'we follow רבי' can be overridden when a later authority like רבא rules the other way.

phrases.english: Even though we hold
that the halacha follows רבי against his colleague,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: here the halacha follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
For רבא said: The halacha is:
from land and not from movable property,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִכְתוּבָּה, בֵּין לִמְזוֹנֵי, בֵּין לְפַרְנָסָה.
phrases.english: whether for a marriage contract, for support, or for a dowry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּקַיְימָא לַן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two opinions just quoted in Steps 6 to 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: collection is only from land, for a כתובה, for מזונות, and for פרנסה.

steps.title: New משנה: a wife gets her basic כתובה even if nothing was written
steps.stepSummary: If the husband wrote no כתובה, a בתולה still collects 200 and an אלמנה a מנה, because it is a תנאי בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not write her a כתובה, a virgin collects 200 and a widow a מנה (100), because it is a condition set by the court.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says the basic כתובה amount does not depend on a written document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The minimum כתובה is not a private deal between husband and wife. בית דין made it a fixed rule, so it applies automatically even if the husband never wrote anything.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract and the money it promises the wife
A condition set by the court that applies automatically

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If he did not write her a marriage contract,
a virgin collects two hundred,
and a widow a maneh,
because it is a condition of the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The minimum כתובה (200 for a בתולה, a מנה for an אלמנה) is owed even without a written document, as a תנאי בית דין.

steps.title: All his property guarantees the full כתובה even if he did not write it
steps.stepSummary: If he wrote her a field worth a מנה in place of 200 זוז and left out the guarantee clause, he still owes the full amount, because it is a תנאי בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote her a field worth a מנה in place of 200 זוז, and did not write 'all my property is a guarantee for your כתובה', he is still obligated, because it is a condition of the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second case. Here the husband wrote a כתובה but tried to limit it to one field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though he named only one field, and one worth less than the full amount, the guarantee on all his property comes automatically from בית דין. He cannot escape paying the full 200 just because he left out the clause.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin; the כתובה is measured in זוז
Guarantors, meaning property that stands as security

phrases.english: If he wrote her a field worth a maneh
in place of two hundred zuz,
and did not write for her
'All property that I have
is a guarantee for your marriage contract'
he is obligated, for it is a condition of the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתַב לָהּ שָׂדֶה שָׁוֶה מָנֶה תַּחַת מָאתַיִם זוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second case of the same משנה, extending תנאי בית דין to the guarantee on all his property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All of the husband's property automatically guarantees the full כתובה, even if he named only one field and left out the guarantee clause.

steps.title: Unwritten promise to redeem a captive wife still binds him
steps.stepSummary: Even if the כתובה left out the promise to redeem her from captivity, or for a כהן's wife the promise to return her home, the husband is obligated, because it is a תנאי בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not write in her כתובה, "If you are taken captive, I will redeem you and take you back as my wife," or for a כהן's wife, "I will return you to your home town," he is still obligated, because the court made this a condition of every marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another automatic כתובה condition. The husband must redeem his captive wife even if he never wrote that promise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as steps 11 and 12. A rule set by בית דין applies whether or not it was written. The כהן's wife gets a different promise, to be brought home, because she cannot go back to living with her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman married to a כהן
A condition the court attached to every marriage

phrases.english: If he did not write for her:
"If you are taken captive, I will redeem you
and settle you back with me as my wife,"
and for a כהן's wife: "I will return you to your province"
he is obligated, because it is a court condition.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא כָּתַב לָהּ אִם תִּשְׁתְּבַאי אֶפְרְקִינִּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another item to the list of unwritten כתובה conditions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband must redeem his captive wife (or return a כהן's wife home) even without a written clause.

steps.title: He cannot divorce her to avoid redeeming her
steps.stepSummary: If his wife was captured he must redeem her. He may not instead hand over a גט and her כתובה money and let her redeem herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was taken captive, he must redeem her. If he says, "Here is her גט and her כתובה money, let her redeem herself," he is not allowed to do that.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules that the husband cannot escape the duty to redeem by divorcing his captive wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The duty to redeem was already in force when she was captured, so a divorce afterward cannot cancel it. This sets up a contrast with healing in the next step.

phrases.english: If she was taken captive, he is obligated to redeem her.
And if he said: Here is her divorce document and her כתובה,
and let her redeem herself,
he is not permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how far the redemption duty from step 13 goes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Divorce cannot be used to avoid the duty to redeem a captive wife.

steps.title: He may divorce her to avoid paying for her healing
steps.stepSummary: If his wife fell ill he must pay for her healing. But if he gives her a גט and her כתובה and lets her heal herself, he is allowed to.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she became sick, he must pay to heal her. If he says, "Here is her גט and her כתובה money, let her heal herself," he is allowed to do that.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה contrasts healing with redemption. Here the husband may end his duty by divorcing her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both healing and redemption are husband's duties. The difference is the outcome: with redemption, divorce does not free him, but with healing it does.

keyTerms.meaning: To heal her, meaning to pay her medical costs

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. For captivity the answer is אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי (not allowed), and for illness it is רַשַּׁאי (allowed).
steps.whatToRemember: Redemption: he cannot escape it by divorce. Healing: he can.

phrases.english: If she was struck with illness, he is obligated to heal her.
If he said: "Here is her divorce document and her כתובה,
let her heal herself," he is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite ruling for illness, as a contrast to captivity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband may divorce his sick wife and pay her כתובה instead of paying for her healing.

steps.title: Who is the author of the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Whose opinion is this משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion by asking who wrote the משנה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the opening line of the משנה (step 11). It treats 200 for a בתולה and a מנה for an אלמנה as a fixed amount set by בית דין. Some תנאים hold that this minimum can never be lowered, and others do not.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
Who is it? Asks whose opinion a teaching follows

phrases.english: GEMARA: Who is it?
phrases.notes: He means: which תנא's opinion is this משנה following?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה into the גמרא's analysis.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the משנה's rule on the minimum כתובה follows.

steps.title: It is רבי מאיר, who forbids giving less than the minimum
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי מאיר. He holds that living with a wife whose כתובה is less than 200 (בתולה) or a מנה (אלמנה) is בעילת זנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי מאיר, who said: Anyone who gives a בתולה less than 200, or an אלמנה less than a מנה, his relationship with her is like בעילת זנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats the minimum כתובה as untouchable: even reducing it with her consent is not allowed. That fits the משנה's opening ruling that a בתולה always collects 200 and an אלמנה a מנה, as fixed court-set amounts.

keyTerms.meaning: A relationship considered licentious, not proper marriage

phrases.english: It is רבי מאיר, who said:
Anyone who reduces a בתולה's sum below two hundred
or a widow's sum below a מנה,
this is licentious relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who forbids any reduction of the minimum כתובה.

steps.title: It cannot be רבי יהודה, who lets the wife waive part
steps.stepSummary: The משנה cannot follow רבי יהודה. He allows a wife to write that she already received half the minimum, so in practice she gets less.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if it were רבי יהודה, he says: if the husband wants, he writes a בתולה a document for 200, and she writes, "I received a מנה from you." For an אלמנה he writes a מנה, and she writes, "I received fifty זוז from you."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves its answer by showing that רבי יהודה's view does not fit the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the minimum can be reduced in practice if the wife agrees to give up part of it in writing. The משנה's opening states fixed amounts (200 and a מנה) that cannot be lowered, so it must follow רבי מאיר instead.

keyTerms.meaning: I have received, a written receipt
A silver coin, also called a dinar

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the minimum כתובה can never be lowered. רבי יהודה: the wife may waive part of it with a receipt. The משנה follows רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: For if it were רבי יהודה, he said:

phrases.aramaic: רָצָה, כּוֹתֵב לִבְתוּלָה שְׁטָר שֶׁל מָאתַיִם,
phrases.english: If he wishes, he writes a בתולה a document for two hundred,
and she writes: "I have received a מנה from you."
phrases.notes: She hasn't really received it; the receipt is her way of giving up half.

phrases.english: And for a widow, he writes a מנה,
and she writes: "I have received fifty zuz from you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 17 by ruling out the other possible author.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה follows רבי מאיר and not רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's ruling that a wife may waive half the minimum with a written receipt, which conflicts with the משנה.

steps.title: The last part of the משנה seems to follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says that if the husband wrote her a field worth a מנה instead of 200 זוז, and did not write that all his property guarantees the כתובה, he still owes the full amount because it is a תנאי בית דין. This fits רבי יהודה, who holds that a missing אחריות clause is a טעות סופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now read the last part of the משנה: If he wrote her a field worth one hundred instead of two hundred זוז, and he did not write for her 'All the property I own is a guarantee for your כתובה,' he is still obligated, because it is a condition set by the court. Here we have come to רבי יהודה, who says that a missing guarantee is a scribe's mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the end of the משנה and points out that it matches רבי יהודה. That is a problem, because the beginning of the same משנה was just shown to follow רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 the רישא was matched to רבי מאיר. The סיפא says his property is tied to the full כתובה even without a written guarantee, and that is רבי יהודה's view that a missing אחריות clause was simply forgotten by the scribe. So one משנה would be following two different תנאים, and the גמרא is raising that difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
A guarantee: property that is tied to a payment
A condition set by the court that applies even if it is not written
The guarantee clause that ties a person's property to a debt
A scribe's mistake: the clause belongs there and was just left out

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two issues. Step 18 was about writing off half the כתובה. This step is about whether his property is tied to the כתובה when no guarantee was written.

phrases.english: Say the last part of the משנה:
If he wrote her a field worth one hundred (a מנה)
instead of two hundred זוז,
phrases.notes: Two hundred זוז is the full כתובה of a בתולה, so the field only covers half.

phrases.english: and he did not write for her
'All the property that I have
is a guarantee for your כתובה' —
he is obligated, because it is a condition of the court.
We have come to רבי יהודה,
who says: a missing guarantee is a scribe's mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having matched the רישא to רבי מאיר, the גמרא shows that the סיפא matches רבי יהודה instead.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from step 17 that the משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא ties his property to the כתובה without a written guarantee. That is רבי יהודה's view, so the משנה would switch תנאים midway.

steps.title: Why the last part cannot be רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא cannot follow רבי מאיר, because he holds that a missing אחריות clause is not a טעות סופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if it were רבי מאיר, he says that a missing guarantee is not a scribe's mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its claim by showing that רבי מאיר holds the opposite of what the סיפא says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, if the guarantee clause is not written, the property is not tied to the debt. The סיפא ties the property anyway, so it cannot be רבי מאיר. That leaves רבי יהודה, which makes the difficulty stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: But he says (pointing to a known opinion)

phrases.english: For if it were רבי מאיר,
he says: a missing guarantee —
is not a scribe's mistake.
phrases.notes: So for רבי מאיר, no written guarantee means his property is not tied to the payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 19 by ruling out רבי מאיר for the סיפא.
steps.raayaObject: That the סיפא must follow רבי יהודה and not רבי מאיר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's known view that a missing אחריות clause is not a טעות סופר

steps.title: The source: the משנה about found loan documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the משנה where רבי מאיר and the other view about אחריות are found: someone who finds loan documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If someone found loan documents, if...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts quoting the משנה that shows where רבי מאיר's opinion about the guarantee comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not just state רבי מאיר's view. It brings the actual source, a משנה about a person who finds loan documents. The rest of that משנה continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
If one found loan documents — if

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the view of רבי מאיר stated in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds a missing אחריות clause is not a טעות סופר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in בבא מציעא about found loan documents
